# KM-143 — Agent client orchestration

**Lane:** agent · **Complexity:** 3 · **Model:** codex · **Depends on:** KM-110, KM-141, KM-142 · **Serializes with:** none
**Plan context (pinned):** [M1 plan](https://github.com/aiur-team/khala/blob/reset/m1-external-plan/docs/plans/2026-10-01-002-refactor-external-m1-thin-path-plan.md) · [contracts](https://github.com/aiur-team/khala/blob/reset/m1-external-plan/docs/build/m1/contracts.md) · [roster and graph](https://github.com/aiur-team/khala/blob/reset/m1-external-plan/docs/build/m1/roster.md)
**Exclusive write surfaces:** `packages/agent/src/client-impl.ts`, `packages/agent/src/client-impl.test.ts`, `packages/agent/src/sender.ts`, `packages/agent/src/sender.test.ts`

## Outcome

`createKhalaAgentClient(...)` returns a working `KhalaAgentClient` (C7). It runs the join handshake (KM-142), starts the Matrix session (KM-110), waits for the owner browser's invite, joins the room, appends other participants' live messages to the inbox (KM-141) with an own-sender filter, reads history, sends, and keeps `status.json` current. Everything is unit-tested against fakes; no live stack needed.

## Context and evidence

- Plan U12 (Agent client core): join → poll 2 s up to 10 min → session → ready → wait for invite → `joinRoom`; intake drops own sender, dedups by `event_id`; send failure writes `status.json`. Requirements R4, R5, R8, R11, R12; KTD1, KTD3, KTD6.
- AE4 (R11): an agent's own message never comes back as an incoming event. With one Matrix account per agent (KTD2), filtering by sender user id is exact.
- Human Matrix ids are opaque `@khala_<base64url>:<server>` (`apps/control/src/composition/human/matrix-identity.ts:9-16`); at `5db209cc` the control participant map uses `displayName: userId` (`apps/control/src/composition/human/matrix.ts:188-197`). In M1, KM-122 sets each human's Matrix display name to `ownerFirstName(verifiedEmail)` at session mint (C4), and agent accounts get the C4 display name `<label> · <ownerFirstName>` (set by KM-132). The agent has no human session cookie, so it cannot call the C3 participants route. Labels therefore come from Matrix member display names via C11 `session.displayName(userId)` (Round 2 R4), with a user-id localpart fallback (C4; see `sender.ts`).
- C7 `join` returns either `awaiting_confirmation` or `connected`. It must return right after the join request; confirmation, credential poll, session start and invite run in the background.

## Scope

1. `sender.ts`: a pure mapping from a decrypted Matrix message to `InboxEntry` (C5), including `senderLabel` and `senderKind`.
2. `client-impl.ts`: `createKhalaAgentClient(options)` implementing `KhalaAgentClient` with an injectable session starter, join API, clock and state directory.
3. Intake cut-off: only messages at or after the agent's own join event reach the inbox. KM-110's `onMessage` enforces it (its ticket, "API"); this client never sees earlier events live. History stays readable through `read()` but never wakes the agent.
4. `status.json` transitions (C5): `idle → joining → connected`, `send_failed`, `disconnected`, with `channelName` once known.
5. An `onInboxAppend` callback for the Codex waker (wired later by KM-150; Round 2 R7).

## Non-goals

- The MCP server, tool schemas, session-id resolution and label defaulting belong to **KM-144**. Wiring this client (and the Codex waker) into `src/mcp/main.ts`, which the KM-103 bin dispatches to (C12), belongs to **KM-150**.
- The Matrix session internals (rust crypto, cross-signing, `joinRoom`, decryption) belong to **KM-110**. State and inbox file I/O belong to **KM-141**. HTTP join calls belong to **KM-142**. Do not edit those files, except to add a missing KM-141/KM-142 export named under "Interface pins" below (see Risks). Never edit `matrix/session.ts`: its surface is C11.
- Hook delivery and cursor advance belong to **KM-145**. Codex `codex queue` belongs to **KM-147**. Channel events (`com.khala.event.v1`) belong to **KM-173/KM-174**: in intake and `read()`, ignore any `SessionMessage` whose `type !== 'm.room.message'` (KM-174 adds event handling).
- Key backup and history after a restart are M2 (deferred finding D1).

### Interface pins (required exports from dependencies)

The session API is contracts.md **C11** (authoritative, quoted verbatim). The other names are pinned here so that sibling tickets converge on them. If a merged KM-141/KM-142 module exports a differently named equivalent, adapt your call sites and record the mapping in the PR body. If a capability is missing entirely, stop (see Risks). Never adapt C11 names: they are fixed.

```ts
// packages/agent/src/client.ts (KM-103): C7 interface, plus this error type (C7, verbatim)
export type KhalaErrorCode = 'invalid_link' | 'link_unavailable' | 'join_expired' | 'not_connected' | 'send_failed' | 'session_unknown' | 'internal_error';
export class KhalaClientError extends Error { readonly code: KhalaErrorCode; constructor(code: KhalaErrorCode, message?: string) }   // KM-103 ships it

// packages/agent/src/matrix/session.ts (KM-110; contracts.md C11, verbatim)
export type SessionMessage = { eventId: string; roomId: string; sender: string; ts: number; type: 'm.room.message' | 'com.khala.event.v1'; body: string; content: Record<string, unknown> };
export interface AgentMatrixSession {
  readonly userId: string;
  onMessage(handler: (m: SessionMessage) => void): () => void;      // excludes own sender; includes com.khala.event.v1
  waitForInvite(roomId: string, timeoutMs: number): Promise<void>;   // resolves once the invite is seen in /sync
  join(roomId: string): Promise<void>;                               // joinRoom, accepting the MSC4268 bundle
  history(roomId: string, limit: number, before?: string): Promise<{ messages: SessionMessage[]; nextBefore?: string }>;
  send(roomId: string, text: string): Promise<{ eventId: string }>;
  sendChannelEvent(roomId: string, content: Record<string, unknown>, txnId?: string): Promise<{ eventId: string }>;
  roomName(roomId: string): string | undefined;
  displayName(userId: string): string | undefined;                  // from room member state; Round 2 R4
  stop(): Promise<void>;
}
export function createAgentMatrixSession(creds: AgentCredentials, opts?: { log?: (line: string) => void }): Promise<AgentMatrixSession>;
// C11: "`displayName(userId)` returns the `displayname` of that user's `m.room.member` state event in the room this session joined,
// read from synced state with no network call. It returns `undefined` when there is no joined room, no member event, or no non-empty
// `displayname`. KM-110 implements it; KM-143 uses it for `senderLabel`, falling back to the user-id localpart (C4)."

// packages/agent/src/state.ts (KM-141)
export function resolveStateDir(harness: Harness, sessionId: string, env?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): string;
export function ensureStateDir(dir: string): Promise<void>;               // mkdir -p, mode 0700
export function writeStateFile(dir: string, name: 'join.json' | 'session.json' | 'cursor.json' | 'status.json', value: unknown): Promise<void>; // atomic, 0600
export function readStateFile<T>(dir: string, name: string): Promise<T | null>;
export function removeStateFile(dir: string, name: string): Promise<void>;

// packages/agent/src/inbox.ts (KM-141; C11 note: `.messages` for wake decisions, `.total` for status)
export function appendInbox(dir: string, entry: InboxEntry): Promise<boolean>; // false when eventId already present
export function unreadCount(dir: string): Promise<{ total: number; messages: number }>;

// packages/agent/src/join.ts (KM-142 owns these; quoted from its ticket)
export function parseChannelLink(link: string): { origin: string } | null;
export function requestJoin(input: { link: string; harness: Harness; label: string }, deps?: { fetch?: typeof fetch }): Promise<AgentJoinCreated & { origin: string }>;
export function pollJoin(input: { origin: string; joinId: string; pollSecret: string }, options?: { intervalMs?: number; timeoutMs?: number; signal?: AbortSignal; fetch?: typeof fetch }): Promise<AgentCredentials>; // throws KhalaClientError('join_expired' | 'link_unavailable')
export function reportReady(input: { origin: string; joinId: string; pollSecret: string }, deps?: { fetch?: typeof fetch }): Promise<void>;
```

**Join errors.** KM-142 already throws `KhalaClientError` (`invalid_link`, `link_unavailable`, `join_expired`, or `internal_error` with a safe reason such as `rate_limited` in `message`). `client-impl.ts` re-throws it unchanged and puts `error.message` (a reason code, never a secret) into `status.json` `detail`. Any other thrown value becomes `KhalaClientError('internal_error')`.

## Contract and invariants

Quoted verbatim from `docs/build/m1/contracts.md`:

> **C5.**
> ```
> $XDG_STATE_HOME/khala/<harness>/<sessionId>/      (default XDG_STATE_HOME = ~/.local/state; dir mode 0700, files 0600)
>   join.json      { joinId, pollSecret, confirmUrl, expiresAt, link }
>   session.json   AgentCredentials (C2)               — deleted on process exit
>   inbox.jsonl    one InboxEntry per line, append-only
>   cursor.json    { lastDeliveredEventId: string | null, deliveredCount: number }
>   status.json    { state: 'idle'|'joining'|'connected'|'send_failed'|'disconnected', channelName?: string, detail?: string, updatedAt: string }
>   activity.json  { state: 'idle'|'busy', updatedAt: string }   — hooks write it; wakers read it; only an idle session is woken
>   watcher.json   { nonce: string, armedAt: string }           — at most one live Claude watcher per session
> ```
> ```ts
> export type InboxEntry = {
>   eventId: string;            // Matrix event id; dedup key
>   roomId: string;
>   ts: string;                 // ISO origin_server_ts
>   sender: string;             // Matrix user id
>   senderLabel: string;        // e.g. "Maya" or "Codex · Maya"
>   senderKind: 'human' | 'agent' | 'unknown';
>   kind: 'message' | 'event';  // 'event' = channel event (events lane), never wakes
>   body: string;               // plaintext; for kind 'event' the formatted line
> };
> ```

> **C7.**
> ```ts
> export interface KhalaAgentClient {
>   join(link: string, label: string): Promise<{ state: 'awaiting_confirmation'; confirmUrl: string } | { state: 'connected'; channelName: string }>;
>   status(): Promise<{ state: string; channelName?: string; agentUserId?: string; unread: number }>;
>   read(limit: number, before?: string): Promise<{ messages: InboxEntry[]; nextBefore?: string }>;
>   send(text: string): Promise<{ eventId: string }>;
>   sendChannelEvent(content: ChannelEventContent): Promise<{ eventId: string }>;   // added by KM-173 (absent before it); errors as send()
>   close(): Promise<void>;
> }
> ```
>
> `status().unread` is KM-141's `unreadCount().total`; wake decisions use `unreadCount().messages` (C11 note).

This ticket implements every member except `sendChannelEvent` (KM-173).

> **C4.** Username: `agent-<ownerHash8>-<rand6>` … Display name: `<label> · <ownerFirstName>`, for example `Claude · Kevin`. … Each process start receives fresh credentials through a fresh join (M1).
> - **Human labels come from Matrix display names, everywhere.** When KM-122 mints a browser session, it sets the human's own Matrix display name to `ownerFirstName(verifiedEmail)`: read it first, write only if different. Readers (control participants, browser, KM-143 agent intake) use the display name. Fallback when it is missing: control's participants `displayName` falls back to the full `matrixUserId` (C3); KM-143's `senderLabel` falls back to the user id localpart.

Invariants:
- I1. `message.sender === session.userId` never reaches `inbox.jsonl` (AE4). C11 `onMessage` already excludes own sender; keep the client-side check as defence in depth.
- I2. An `eventId` is appended at most once. `appendInbox` dedups; the client does not keep a second dedup set.
- I3. Only messages at or after the agent's own join event are appended; KM-110's `onMessage` guarantees this. Earlier messages are history: `read()` returns them, but they never wake the agent.
- I4. Access tokens are written only to `session.json` (0600). They never go into `status.json` `detail`, thrown messages or logs.
- I5. `status.json` is written exactly in the C5 shape, with `updatedAt` as an ISO string from the injected clock.

## Implementation pointers (refreshable @ 5db209cc)

### Files

- Create `packages/agent/src/sender.ts`, `packages/agent/src/sender.test.ts`, `packages/agent/src/client-impl.ts` and `packages/agent/src/client-impl.test.ts`.
- Modify nothing else. If `@khala/contracts` is not yet a dependency of `packages/agent/package.json`, stop: KM-103/KM-141 own that file.

### Worked example

Live `SessionMessage` from a human, received by the agent `@agent-1a2b3c4d-x9y8z7:khala.local` after its join:

```json
{ "eventId": "$ev1", "roomId": "!room:khala.local", "ts": 1790935500000, "sender": "@khala_b3duxzq:khala.local",
  "type": "m.room.message", "body": "Docs are a go from my side.", "content": { "msgtype": "m.text", "body": "Docs are a go from my side." } }
```
with `session.displayName('@khala_b3duxzq:khala.local')` returning `undefined` (no display name set yet), becomes this appended line:
```json
{"eventId":"$ev1","roomId":"!room:khala.local","ts":"2026-10-02T10:05:00.000Z","sender":"@khala_b3duxzq:khala.local","senderLabel":"khala_b3duxzq","senderKind":"human","kind":"message","body":"Docs are a go from my side."}
```
When `session.displayName(...)` returns `'Maya'` (KM-122 set it), `toInboxEntry(message, 'Maya')` gives `senderLabel: "Maya"`. A message from `@agent-9f8e7d6c-abc123:khala.local` with display name `"Codex · Maya"` maps to `senderLabel: "Codex · Maya"` and `senderKind: "agent"`. A `type: 'com.khala.event.v1'` message is ignored here.

### Steps

1. **`sender.ts`.** Export `toInboxEntry(message: SessionMessage, displayName?: string | null): InboxEntry` and `senderKindOf(userId: string): 'human' | 'agent' | 'unknown'`.
   - Kind: a localpart starting `agent-` gives `agent`; one starting `khala_` gives `human`; anything else gives `unknown`.
   - Label: use `displayName` when it is non-empty and differs from `sender`. Otherwise use the localpart, which is the text between `@` and the first `:`.
   - Body: `message.body`. (C11 history omits undecryptable events, so there is no failure marker to map.)
   - `ts` is `new Date(ms).toISOString()`; `kind` is always `'message'`.
   - `client-impl.ts` passes `session.displayName(message.sender)` (C11, Round 2 R4) for every mapped message, in intake and in `read()`.
2. **Options type** in `client-impl.ts`:
   ```ts
   export type KhalaAgentClientOptions = { harness: Harness; sessionId: string; env?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv;
     now?: () => Date; startSession?: typeof createAgentMatrixSession;
     joinApi?: { requestJoin: typeof requestJoin; pollJoin: typeof pollJoin; reportReady: typeof reportReady };
     fetch?: typeof fetch;
     inviteTimeoutMs?: number /* default 120_000 */; onInboxAppend?: (entry: InboxEntry) => void };
   export function createKhalaAgentClient(options: KhalaAgentClientOptions): KhalaAgentClient;
   ```
   On creation, compute the directory with `resolveStateDir`. Lazily, on the first method call, run `ensureStateDir` and write `status.json` `{state:'idle'}`.
3. **`join(link, label)`:**
   - (a) If connected, return `{state:'connected', channelName}`. M1 has one channel per session.
   - (b) If a background join is in flight for the same `link`, return `{state:'awaiting_confirmation', confirmUrl}` from memory.
   - (c) If `join.json` exists for the same `link` but no join is in flight, check its `expiresAt`. If it is `<= now`: remove `join.json`, set status `{state:'idle', detail:'join_expired'}`, and throw `KhalaClientError('join_expired')`. That gives the agent an explicit "ask again" signal. Otherwise fall through to (d); the server join can no longer be resumed without its poller.
   - (d) If a join is in flight for a different link, abort it with its `AbortController`. Then call `created = await requestJoin({link, harness, label}, { fetch })` and write `join.json` as the C5 shape `{ joinId, pollSecret, confirmUrl, expiresAt, link }` via `writeStateFile(dir, 'join.json', …)`; keep `created.origin` in memory. Errors per "Join errors" above. Set status `joining`, start `runBackgroundJoin(created)` without awaiting it, and return `{state:'awaiting_confirmation', confirmUrl}`.
4. **`runBackgroundJoin(created)`** runs these steps in order:
   1. `pollJoin({ origin, joinId, pollSecret }, { signal, fetch })`. It polls every 2 s and gives up after 10 minutes (KM-142 defaults).
   2. Write `session.json` (credentials).
   3. `startSession(credentials)`.
   4. Subscribe `onMessage` (step 5).
   5. `reportReady({ origin, joinId, pollSecret }, { fetch })`.
   6. `waitForInvite(roomId, inviteTimeoutMs)`.
   7. `join(roomId)`, then mark the room joined.
   8. `channelName = roomName(roomId) ?? roomId`.
   9. Remove `join.json`, then set status `{ state: 'connected', channelName }`.

   On any failure: `join_expired` becomes status `idle`/`join_expired`; an invite timeout becomes `disconnected`/`invite_timeout`; anything else becomes `disconnected`/`<code or 'internal_error'>`. On any failure, also stop a started session and remove `session.json`. Never reject an unhandled promise: catch inside.
5. **Intake listener:**
   - Drop the message if `message.type !== 'm.room.message'`, if `message.roomId !== credentials.roomId`, or if `message.sender === session.userId` (I1). The join cut-off (I3) is KM-110's.
   - While `join` is still pending, buffer messages in memory. Replay them through these same rules right after `join` resolves, so a live message that races the join is not lost.
   - Otherwise `appendInbox(dir, toInboxEntry(message, session.displayName(message.sender)))`. When it returns `true`, call `onInboxAppend?.(entry)` inside a try/catch.
   - Serialize appends through a promise chain so order is preserved.
6. **`read(limit, before)`:**
   - If not connected, throw `not_connected`.
   - Otherwise call `session.history(roomId, limit, before)`, keep `type === 'm.room.message'`, map each with `toInboxEntry(m, session.displayName(m.sender))` (own messages included, since this is a read of the channel), and return `{messages}` plus the session's `nextBefore` when present.
7. **`send(text)`:**
   - If not connected, throw `not_connected`.
   - Call `session.send(roomId, text)`. On success, return `{eventId}` and set status `connected` if it was `send_failed`.
   - On a thrown error, set status `{state:'send_failed', detail:'send_failed'}` and throw `KhalaClientError('send_failed')`. Do not include the original message; it may echo the token or URL.
8. **Sync state:** C11 has no sync-state listener; this client does not track sync errors (`status.json` changes only on the transitions in steps 3–7 and 10).
9. **`status()`:** returns `{state, channelName?, agentUserId?, unread: (await unreadCount(dir)).total}`. The state comes from memory and mirrors `status.json`.
10. **`close()`:** idempotent. Abort the background join, `session.stop()`, `removeStateFile(dir,'session.json')`, and set status `disconnected`/`closed`.
11. Every `status.json` write after the room is known includes `channelName` (C5).

## Test scenarios

`packages/agent/src/sender.test.ts`:
1. `@khala_abc:khala.local`, display name null → `senderLabel 'khala_abc'`, `senderKind 'human'`.
2. `@agent-1a2b3c4d-x9y8z7:khala.local`, display name `Codex · Maya` → `'Codex · Maya'`, `'agent'`.
3. `@bob:example.org`, display name equal to the user id → `'bob'`, `'unknown'`.
4. `@khala_abc:khala.local`, display name `Maya` → `senderLabel 'Maya'` (A3).
5. `ts` of 1790935500000 → `'2026-10-02T10:05:00.000Z'`.

`packages/agent/src/client-impl.test.ts`: use a temp `XDG_STATE_HOME` (`fs.mkdtemp`), a fake session (an EventEmitter-backed object implementing `AgentMatrixSession`), fake join API functions, and a fixed clock.
1. `join` returns `awaiting_confirmation` with the fake `confirmUrl`. `join.json` exists with mode `0o600` and the directory has mode `0o700`; status is `joining`.
2. The background completes in order: credentials → `startSession` → `reportReady` → `waitForInvite` → `join`. Then `status()` is `{state:'connected', channelName:'Release room', agentUserId, unread:0}`, `status.json` has `channelName: 'Release room'`, `session.json` exists, and `join.json` is gone.
3. A second `join` with the same link while pending → same `confirmUrl`, `requestJoin` called once.
4. `join` after connected → `{state:'connected', channelName}`.
5. `pollJoin` rejects `KhalaClientError('join_expired', 'expired')` → status `idle`/`join_expired`. A stale `join.json` with a past `expiresAt` plus a new client → `join` throws `join_expired`; the next `join` calls `requestJoin` again.
6. `requestJoin` rejects `KhalaClientError('invalid_link')` → `join` rejects with code `invalid_link`; `KhalaClientError('internal_error', 'rate_limited')` → code `internal_error`, and status `detail` is `rate_limited`. A plain `Error('x')` → `internal_error`.
7. Own-sender message after the join (the fake emits it despite C11) → not in `inbox.jsonl`, and `onInboxAppend` is not called (Covers AE4).
8. The same event emitted twice → one line, one `onInboxAppend` call.
9. A pre-join message present only in the fake `history` → not appended, but returned by `read` (Covers AE1 shape).
10. Three live messages emitted quickly → appended in emit order.
11. `send` before connected → `not_connected`. Session `send` rejects → `send_failed` thrown, and `status.json` is `send_failed`. The next successful send → `connected`.
12. `read(2)` with the fake history returning `nextBefore: '$old'` → two entries and `nextBefore: '$old'`; without it → no `nextBefore` key.
13. `waitForInvite` rejects → status `disconnected`/`invite_timeout`; `session.stop` called; `session.json` removed.
14. `close()` twice → `stop` called once, `session.json` absent, status `disconnected`.
15. A `type: 'com.khala.event.v1'` live message → not appended; one in `history` → not returned by `read`.
16. A message emitted while the fake `join` is still pending → appended once after `join` resolves.
17. `status().unread` equals the fake/real `unreadCount().total` (with one message and one `kind:'event'` entry in the inbox → `2`).
18. Labels (Round 2 R4): the fake session's `displayName` returns `'Maya'` for `@khala_abc:khala.local` and `undefined` for `@khala_xyz:khala.local`. A live message from each → inbox `senderLabel` `'Maya'` and `'khala_xyz'`. `read()` maps history entries the same way.

Done means both commands are green, and `createKhalaAgentClient` is exported from `packages/agent/src/client-impl.ts` and satisfies `KhalaAgentClient` (add `const _check: KhalaAgentClient = createKhalaAgentClient(...)` in a test).

## Risks and stop conditions

- **Stop** if KM-110's `session.ts` does not match C11, or its `onMessage` delivers pre-join events. Ask the Executor; do not reach into matrix-js-sdk from this file.
- **Stop** if `KhalaClientError` is absent from `client.ts`. Do not create a second error type.
- **Display names (resolved, Round 2 R4).** C11 now has `displayName(userId)`; use it as in steps 1, 5 and 6. **Stop** if KM-110's merged `session.ts` lacks it. Do not call the control participants route.

## Complexity rationale

3: an async state machine with a background flow, abort handling, and five collaborators behind pins. It is pure orchestration, with no crypto or HTTP of its own.
